items.title: PNB unit eyes up to RM600mil recurring annual income from Merdeka 118
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd expects recurring income from the completed Merdeka 118 development to reach RM500 million-RM600 million a year over the medium term. This shields PNB Merdeka from occupancy and most property-related cost risks. MARC has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka's RM6 billion Merdeka sukuk Wakalah with a stable outlook.

items.title: Indonesia warned to keep its guard against wildfire despite drop in hotspots
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Indonesian government must keep its guard up against wildfires despite a recent decline in the number of hotspots, with peatland fires still prone to flare up amid persistently hot and dry weather, environmental groups said on Monday. Though Indonesia's Forestry Ministry said the number of hotspots had nearly halved from Friday to Saturday, there was still high potential for peatland fires, said Putra Saptian, a campaigner with the peatland protection group Pantau Gambut. "The nature of (peatland) fires, which spread through underground organic material, can trigger persistent smouldering and create the potential for fires to re-emerge," he said.

items.title: ParkIt says RM5 'fee' collection at MRT facility not by its employees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ParkIt Malaysia has denied any involvement in the collection of a RM5 "parking fee" by an unidentified person at the Maluri Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) Park and Ride facility here. "ParkIt does not collect any parking fees at Maluri MRT at present and does not authorise any party to collect payments on our behalf," it said. It also referred the incident to MRT Corp, Rapid KL, police and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL).

items.title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.

items.title: Cognitive warfare aims to blur line between truth and falsehood, says Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cognitive warfare is no longer simply about spreading fake news, but about undermining people's ability to distinguish between what is true and false, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. He said malicious actors could use fabricated content, false authorities, fake news platforms and manipulated social media engagement to create an entire ecosystem of deception. Khaled said these developments demonstrated how closely cyber capabilities and cognitive resilience were interconnected.

items.title: Finnish town braces for change from Google data centres
items.summary: IN the northern Finnish town of Muhos, 36-year-old farmer Joni Pitkanen is preparing for life with a new neighbour – just kilometres away, tech giant Google is planning to build new data centres. The planned data centres are part of an announced 13-billion-euro (US$15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years – the US tech giant's single biggest investment in Europe. Google's expansion plans include the Finnish municipalities of Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala as well as Hamina, where it already operates a data centre.

items.title: Government looking into caning mule account holders
items.summary: Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the proposal was put forward to address the threat posed by financial fraud syndicates, which have become increasingly complex. Meanwhile, Shamsul Anuar revealed that the police had conducted 100,230 raids on fraud syndicate call centres between 2023 and August, resulting in the arrest of 9,159 individuals across the entire chain of syndicates. "These statistics demonstrate that police continue to intensify enforcement actions to cripple the entire operational chain of these fraud syndicates," he said.

items.title: Johor MB: State government ready to help schools review security measures following student’s death
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The Johor state government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz expressed full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry (MOE), particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within school premises. Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD).

items.title: Lawmaker says foreign doctors could help ease Sabah, Sarawak shortage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consider recruiting foreign doctors to address shortages of medical officers in Sabah and Sarawak, said Bandar Kuching member of parliament Dr Kelvin Yii. The rate of medical officers who failed to report for permanent appointments had risen from 2 per cent in 2022 to 20 per cent in 2023, around 40 per cent in 2025 and 66 per cent for hospital postings in Sabah this month, he said. He said Kudat Hospital received four of 17 doctors, while Sri Aman Hospital received six of 20.

items.title: Takiyuddin questions RM193.71mil court bail funds held in private account
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should explain the status of RM193.71 million in court bail funds held in a private company's bank account instead of being transferred to the Consolidated Trust Account, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Baru) said. He also questioned how the company had been allowed to handle court bail transactions for five years without a formal contract with the government. "How could a company manage public money transactions for five years without a contract?"

items.title: NRES: No more exemptions for companies which fail to meet emission standards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Companies that fail to take concrete steps to reduce emissions will no longer be granted exemptions under the Environmental Quality (Clean Air) Regulations. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said all companies must comply with emission standards by 2030. Arthur said exemptions would only be granted to companies that had demonstrated steps towards implementing the necessary technology for cleaner emissions.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says joined Yemen govt offensive against Houthis
items.summary: RIYADH: The Saudi-led military coalition announced on Monday its participation in the new Yemen government offensive targeting the Iran-backed Houthis, with 100 warplanes used in dawn strikes to provide air cover for ground forces. "100 fighter jets participated at dawn today in Operation 'Dawn of Yemen'," coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki wrote on X, using the name for the new offensive announced on Sunday. The coalition's announcement came after the Yemeni military said it launched a broad set of strikes against Houthi targets on Monday, after the country's internationally recognised government declared a new campaign to retake all territory.

items.title: PM Anwar: Land encroachment must be taken seriously
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Good governance practices must continue to be upheld, while any form of unauthorised land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he stressed these points while chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting. “Land management must be carried out prudently and systematically to minimise risks to environmental sustainability,” he said.

items.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor takes police to court over Epstein files arrest
items.summary: LONDON: King Charles' younger brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, is taking the police to court to challenge his arrest in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations he sent confidential government documents to Jeffrey Epstein. Britain's Judicial Office, part of the non-political civil service which supports the courts, said on Monday a hearing would take place on Thursday after the former prince sought to quash the search warrants that were issued as part of the arrest. Thames Valley Police, which carried out the arrest, confirmed it was engaged in legal proceedings and declined further comment.

items.title: Fix Sabah, Sarawak doctor shortage with better incentives, parliamentary committee tells MOH
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health wants the Health Ministry to review existing allowances and incentives to encourage medical officers to serve in Sabah and Sarawak. Special Select Committee on Health member Young Syefura Othman said the refusal of medical officers to take up postings in the two states was a serious concern, with some hospitals operating with as few as three medical officers. "Therefore, committee members want the ministry to review the existing schemes and consider fair and meaningful incentives," she said.

items.title: e-Jamin: Why is the bail system under scrutiny?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) found that the e-Jamin system had operated for five years without a formal government contract and raised concerns about the handling of bail deposits, including funds held in the operator's commercial accounts. The e-Jamin system is an electronic court bail payment service that allows a surety, or bailor, to pay bail online on behalf of an accused person. Under the conventional bail process, a surety may have to arrange payment through a bank before the accused can be released on bail.

items.title: IGP: Intelligence gathering, surveillance part of TCO duties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Travel Control Officers (TCO) are tasked with intelligence-related duties, including establishing contact with certain parties and conducting surveillance, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said. Khalid, responding to questions about the role of TCOs following an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, said the officers came under the Special Branch. He said intelligence gathering could involve officers establishing contact with certain parties, conducting surveillance and carrying out other operational duties.

items.title: IGP: No confirmation yet of SOP breach in KLIA altercation video
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are uncertain if any procedural breaches took place during the viral altercation involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain and Travel Control Officers (TCO) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, explaining the role of the Special Branch's TCOs, said they carry out intelligence-related duties, including establishing contact with certain parties and surveillance. Let the investigation be completed," he said.

items.title: Zetrix AI in discussions to resolve issues as JPJ services temporarily suspended
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd said it is currently in discussions to resolve issues with the Road Transport Department (JPJ) following the temporary suspension of its services to the department effective today. The company confirmed in a stock exchange filing today that JPJ services would be temporarily suspended effective Oct 5, 2026. On Oct 2, JPJ announced that services provided by MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd under the MYEG Group as its collection agents would be suspended from 12.01 am on Oct 5.

items.title: Warehouse worker pleads not guilty to driving under the influence, injuring two marathon runners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 —An e-commerce platform warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol, causing injuries to two participants of a running event last Saturday. Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation, representing Muhammad Saiful, appealed for a bail reduction, saying that his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar granted Muhammad Saiful bail of RM500 with one surety for each charge and set Jan 7, 2027, for case mention and submission of documents.

items.title: India court seeks explanations from election body in voter list row
items.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Supreme Court ordered the government and the national election body on Monday to explain decisions linked to a large-scale revision of voter rolls that prompted accusations of wrongdoing. Opposition parties and activists have organised protests and called for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, head of the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging that the revision had improperly removed millions of names from voter lists. On Monday, a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notices to the government, the ECI and Kumar after hearing petitions challenging decisions linked to the voter list revision.

items.title: Genting founder's grandson seeks removal of late mother's RM1.6b estate administrators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The interim administrators of late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim's RM1.6 billion estate allegedly paid lawyers over RM2 million without approval, breaching a court order, the High Court heard today. The administrators, lawyer Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat were appointed by the High Court on Nov 27, 2023, to manage the estate administrators pendente lite amid an ongoing family dispute over the validity of Siew Kim's will. He said the payments were allegedly made despite an earlier court order requiring payments relating to debts other than those of Siew Kim to be subjected to the court's scrutiny.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia must move beyond traditional manufacturing, strengthen AI capabilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must move beyond traditional manufacturing and strengthen its capabilities in high-end technology, particularly artificial intelligence. In a Facebook post, he said he held discussions with prominent figures from the technology and academic sectors at the Khazanah Megatrends Forum 2026, where technological transformation, geopolitics and Malaysia's economic future were discussed. He said discussions with semiconductor industry leader Datuk Fong Swee Kiang centred on the need for Malaysia to strengthen its capabilities in high-end technology and benefit from the ongoing AI-driven technological transformation.

items.title: Defence Ministry seeks more funding in 2027 Budget
items.summary: He said the allocation should take into account the country's needs, particularly to ensure that the armed forces had sufficient capabilities to defend the country and safeguard its sovereignty. "I believe the Prime Minister will give due consideration based on the country's needs and our need to defend the country and safeguard its sovereignty. On Aug 7, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would continue efforts to increase defence allocations through the 2027 Budget to strengthen the armed forces' readiness and ensure the welfare of security personnel.

items.title: Man charged with murder of Indian domestic helper
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman was charged at the magistrate's court here today with murdering his domestic helper last month. Stevent Anthony, 31, was accused of murdering Tamilarasi Kumar, an Indian citizen, at a house in Titiwangsa between 4am and 10.55am on Sept 24. The accused nodded to indicate that he understood the charge, which was read out in court.

items.title: IJM appoints former KPMG Malaysia managing partner Johan Idris as chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR:IJM Corp Bhd has appointed Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman of the board, effective today. Commenting on his appointment, Johan said he is honoured to join the IJM board and take on the role of chairman. "I welcome Johan to the IJM board and as chairman.

items.title: AG's Report: Six 12MP projects face delays, contract terminations
items.summary: According to the Auditor General's Report 2/2026, the six projects comprised two Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) projects, the Galeria Perdana upgrading project in Langkawi, a People's Housing Programme (PPR) project and two fire station quarters projects in Sabah. The first one, the RM100 million Joint Task Force 2 (ATB 2) RKAT project at Kukusan Camp, Tawau, Sabah, originally scheduled for completion in July 2024, achieved only 28 per cent physical progress as of Dec 31, 2024. Meanwhile, a RM63.25 million Air Force Base Quarters project in Labuan was granted four EOTs totalling 467 days up to 2025, followed by two additional EOTs totalling 410 days in 2026, with the completion date extended to Nov 17.

items.title: Irene's grandfather urges action against those responsible for her death
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The grandfather of 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Kharool Faisal expressed deep grief today over the death of his granddaughter, who was found dead in a school hall in Yong Peng. Khyar Abas, 69, struggled to hide his heartbreak over the tragic loss of his granddaughter, affectionately known as Fiya. Even if I cry, Fiya will not return.

items.title: MPs seek answers on Flying Doctor Service safety after Sarawak crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two members of parliament have raised concerns over the safety and continuity of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following last month's helicopter crash that killed five people in Long Lellang, Sarawak. Dr Kelvin Yii (PH-Bandar Kuching) questioned the use of a 35-year-old Bo 105 helicopter for the service, as well as the maintenance oversight of aircraft operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace. He also asked whether the contract stipulated an age limit for aircraft used in the service, and when the Health Ministry last independently audited the company's maintenance records.

items.title: Govt launches framework to prepare communications, multimedia workforce for AI-driven changes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The federal government today launched a new framework to align communications and multimedia industry needs with education and skills development as artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, emerging technologies and the green economy reshape the sector. Its implementation will also involve the Higher Education and Human Resources ministries to align industry needs with education and skills development. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the framework identifies industry needs while aligning government, industry and education efforts to keep talent development in step with technological and economic changes.

items.title: PN says suspension could shut coalition out of Melaka polls
items.summary: The coalition said in court papers that the suspension prevents it from carrying out normal political activities, including authorising candidates to contest under the PN banner and using its registered name and symbol. PN said any court decision in its favour after nomination day could come too late as the opportunity to field candidates under the coalition's banner could no longer be restored. The matter was raised in a certificate of urgency filed together with PN's judicial review application challenging two notices issued by RoS.

items.title: Good governance key to curbing illegal land encroachment, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Good governance and strong enforcement are needed to curb illegal land encroachment, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Speaking after chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting, Anwar said issues raised by stakeholders, including non-governmental organisations, must be addressed promptly to ensure accurate and transparent communication. "Good governance must continue to be upheld and any form of illegal land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: MPs urge Home Ministry to take over refugee registration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Government and opposition members of Parliament have urged that the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) no longer be given the mandate to register refugees in the country. Lawmaker RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) said the Home Ministry should be given full responsibility for refugee registration, alongside an integrated nationwide operation to monitor their whereabouts. "Who gave UNHCR such extensive authority that some refugees believe they are free to do anything with a UNHCR refugee card?

items.title: Zara inquest: Coroner conducts second site visit to teen's school
items.summary: PAPAR: The Coroner's Court today conducted a second site visit to SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha as part of an inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir. Several adult witnesses, including teachers, and child witnesses attended the visit to clarify locations, layout, and physical conditions mentioned in earlier testimony. The court conducted its first visit on Sept 11 last year.

items.title: TA Securities to underwrite SKA Capital's Malaysian public portion in ACE Market IPO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SKA Capital Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with TA Securities Holdings Bhd for its proposed listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia, where the stock broking company will underwrite the entire portion of the new shares offered to the Malaysian public investors and eligible persons. The initial public offering (IPO) involves a public issue of 168.08 million new shares and an offer for sale of 72.4 million existing shares. SKA Capital, through its subsidiaries SKA Rekabina and Reltency Engineering, provides power infrastructure engineering services, including substation engineering, engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning, civil and structural engineering, electrical and mechanical engineering, and underground utilities engineering.

items.title: ‘Touch ‘n Go rep’ scam leaves Kedah woman RM150 poorer, says consumer group
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 5 — A 39-year-old self-employed woman lost about RM150, including her BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) petrol subsidy and reward points, after a phone scammer posing as a Touch ‘n Go representative compromised her e-wallet. Kedah Consumers Association (Cake) president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said the victim lodged a report at the association’s office yesterday. “The victim said the caller offered her a new Touch ‘n Go card with various perks, including reward points, store vouchers offering discounts of up to 80 per cent, and overseas spending capabilities.

items.title: Penang stays on alert for human rabies after Kedah man dies of infection
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Penang has recorded no human rabies cases since the last two cases were reported in 1975, with the Penang State Health Department remaining on standby to respond to any possible cases. State Youth, Sports and Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi Zi Sen said no animal rabies cases had also been detected in the state to date. Gooi said the state government was also working with the Department of Veterinary Services to monitor the rabies situation in Penang.

items.title: High Court rejects Bar bid to challenge Ahmad Terrirudin’s JAC appointment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The High Court today dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings challenging the appointment of Federal Court judge Ahmad Terrirudin Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC), according to a report by Free Malaysia Today (FMT). Justice Norliza Othman, in delivering her decision, held that Section 5(1)(e) of the JAC Act 2009 was unambiguous. Terrirudin, a former attorney-general, was elevated to the Federal Court in November 2024.

items.title: Woman, 69, found dead in parked car after discharge from Melaka Hospital
items.summary: Melaka Tengah district police chief ACP Halim Abas said in a statement today that the woman was found at about 4pm after she was discharged from Melaka Hospital, still wearing hospital clothes with her left arm in a sling. Her 44-year-old son received a call from Melaka Hospital at 1.50pm to take her home. She was wearing hospital clothes as she had no spare clothes,” he said.

items.title: Electric buses hit the test track as Rapid Penang gears up for greener rides
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Rapid Penang will conduct test runs of two electric buses on Oct 6 and 7, marking an initial step towards the introduction of electric buses into Penang’s public transport system. In a statement today, Rapid Penang said the initiative was part of Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd’s ongoing efforts to replace existing buses with safer, more sustainable and environmentally friendly vehicles, while enhancing operational efficiency. “The test run involves two electric buses from different manufacturers, namely a 12-metre Foton bus and an 8.25-metre Golden Dragon bus.

items.title: PAS MP calls for humane approach to Rohingya refugees amid calls for tighter controls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — PAS lawmaker Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman today called on the government to strike a balance in managing Rohingya refugees, saying a strict immigration policy must also be humane. “We must protect national security, control our borders, and maintain strong registration systems, but in doing so, we cannot lose our humanity and sense of justice,” Sik MP Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman said when addressing the House during a debate on refugee management. Such a system, he said, would properly distinguish genuine refugees from economic migrants, undocumented immigrants and victims of human trafficking.

items.title: Malaysia’s statutory debt at RM1.295t, or 63.9pc of GDP, still within legal limit, says Auditor General’s report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Federal Government’s statutory debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 63.9 per cent last year, remaining below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, according to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026. According to the report, the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills. “This ratio remains below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, as stipulated under the Loans (Local) (Statutory Limit on Borrowing) and Government Funding (Statutory Limit on Moneys Received) Order 2022,” it said.

items.title: Chicken curry, evening drives and a white cat: Song Swee Guan’s family remembers the man behind the Sarawak politician
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 5 — Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan has been remembered as a selfless and caring man who was able to balance between work and family. According to Song’s niece Kaylene Tan, his dedication to his work and selfless care for his parents kept him single. Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan was known to be a good cook by family members.

items.title: Planes, not just ships: Myanmar says most migrants returned from Malaysia flew home, as UN criticises Putrajaya’s scheme
items.summary: YANGON, Oct 5 — Myanmar has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, state media said on Monday, a day after a flotilla returning almost 1,500 of its citizens docked in the country. The United Nations (UN) has sharply criticised Malaysia’s push to return migrants to Myanmar under an opaque scheme it says cannot guarantee safe homecomings to the war-torn nation. A group of 1,476 returnees arrived by ship outside Yangon on Sunday, the first of 5,000 that Kuala Lumpur says Myanmar agreed to take back amid a wave of anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.

items.title: Targeted subsidy reforms help cut Malaysia’s 2025 bill by RM15.67b, federal audit shows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government has managed to reduce its subsidy expenditure by 40.1 per cent to RM23.43 billion in 2025 from RM39.10 billion in 2024, supported by the decline in crude oil prices and the implementation of the targeted diesel and petrol subsidy reforms. Petrol subsidy expenditure fell 46.5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) to RM10.51 billion from RM19.66 billion in 2024, while diesel subsidy expenditure declined 48.2 per cent y-o-y to RM5.98 billion from RM11.54 billion previously. Meanwhile, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) subsidy expenditure decreased 29.1 per cent y-o-y to RM2.63 billion from RM3.71 billion previously.

items.title: State audits flag governance weaknesses despite clean financial opinions
items.summary: The National Audit Department (JAN), in a statement regarding the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 today, announced that these findings follow the completion of audits on all 13 State Government Financial Statements for the year ending Dec 31, 2025. JAN also issued Auditor General’s Certificates for 298 State Agencies for the 2024 financial year and reported the results of performance audits conducted on 22 State Government programmes and activities. LKAN 2/2026, covering the Federal Government Financial Statements for 2025, activities of Federal Government Ministries/Departments, State Government and State Agency Financial Statements, activities of State Ministries/Departments/Agencies, and the management of State Government-owned companies, was tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Govt’s dividend income edges up 1.4pc to RM39.55b, with Petronas paying most of it, says A-G
items.summary: Based on the report, BNM’s dividend increased to RM5.25 billion in 2025 from RM2.85 billion in 2024, while Khazanah Nasional Bhd’s dividend increased to RM2 billion in 2025 from RM1 billion in 2024. The total dividends of statutory bodies increased by 81.8 per cent to RM5.275 billion from RM2.902 billion, while the total dividends of companies decreased by 5.1 per cent to RM34.271 billion from RM36.109 billion. “Overall, the dividend receipts from nine companies and one statutory body amounted to RM7.433 billion compared to RM3.982 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.451 billion (86.7 per cent).

items.title: Prosecution to call up to 20 witnesses as GISBH money laundering trial proceeds at Shah Alam court
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — The Sessions Court here was informed today that the representation submitted by the former chief executive officer (CEO) of GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and three former company accountants to drop money laundering charges against them had been rejected. Following this, Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Ashrof Adrin, who appeared alongside DPP Muhamad Ehsan Nasarudin, said the prosecution would proceed with the trial. The four accused are Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, facing 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, facing 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, facing 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million.

items.title: Binning edible food a ‘grave sin’, says housing minister as nearly 16,000 tonnes tossed daily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Nearly 40 per cent of the 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said this when replying to a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and increase recycling rates. Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition involving 1,680 schools successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million.

items.title: No mandatory e-Consular registration yet, but foreign minister wants Malaysians abroad to sign up to make contact in emergencies easier
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government does not yet intend to make registration on the e-Consular system mandatory for Malaysians abroad, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said registration through the digital platform managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs remains voluntary, but Malaysians residing, travelling or studying abroad are highly encouraged to register to facilitate monitoring and welfare matters. “Not yet (making registration mandatory).

items.title: Record RM4.64b income, highest payout in eight years: Zulkifli Hasan says Tabung Haji’s governance now stronger
items.summary: This development is reflected, among other things, in TH recording its highest investment income in history, he said. Zulkifli said TH has a systematic investment process, which includes assessing investment, risk and shariah aspects before making any investment decision. For the 2025 financial year, TH’s investment income rose to RM4.64 billion, the highest level recorded.

items.title: Police vow no cover-up in probe into schoolgirl’s death in Yong Peng
items.summary: Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigation would be conducted comprehensively and professionally, with no attempt to cover up the case or protect any party. Police said the school and Education Ministry were cooperating fully with the investigation. The case remains under investigation.

items.title: Yong Peng school had CCTV but none at the crime scene, security firm under probe, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The secondary school in Yong Peng, Johor, where a Form Four female student was allegedly found murdered, is equipped with CCTV cameras, but none were installed at the location where the incident occurred. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Ministry of Education (MOE) is now upgrading the CCTV facilities and has launched an investigation into the school’s security company to determine whether there were any breaches of standard operating procedures (SOPs). Justice for Irene Sofiya,” she said.

items.title: RM68.81m in contractor advance payments still unrecovered, Audit Dept finds
items.summary: “RM59.63 million out of RM68.81 million in WPK receivables outstanding for more than 10 years involved 21 companies,” the report read. The report stated that five of the companies had been dissolved, involving WPK receivables amounting to RM10.68 million, while 13 companies had been wound up, involving outstanding WPK of RM27.76 million. Another three companies remained active, with outstanding WPK amounting to RM21.19 million.

items.title: Puspakom opens Kajang centre with capacity to inspect 800 vehicles daily
items.summary: KAJANG, Oct 5 — Puspakom Sdn Bhd today began operations at its new inspection centre in Bandar Teknologi Kajang, with the facility eventually able to handle up to 800 vehicles a day. Private vehicle inspections began today, while Routine and Re-Routine inspections for light commercial vehicles will be introduced on October 28, followed by Initial and Re-Initial inspections from November 23. Puspakom said the phased opening was aimed at ensuring operational readiness while providing customers with a smoother inspection experience.

items.title: Perikatan parties file judicial review challenging ROS suspension, show-cause letter
items.summary: PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the application for judicial review was filed by the secretary-generals of all PN component parties. Takiyuddin said the coalition wants the judicial review application to be expedited given that the Melaka state election is approaching. Coalition leaders said the ROS suspension could disrupt PN’s preparations for the Melaka state polls, with it still unclear whether the coalition can contest under its own banner.

items.title: ‘Who sent the threats?’ Businessman seeks answers from police a year after Caprice case classified NFA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Maritime industry executive Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan, who was investigated over alleged threats made against social media influencer Caprice and his family, wants to know whether anyone has since been identified as being behind the threats. The chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said a year had passed since Caprice lodged the complaint against him, and it was important for him to know the outcome, particularly as he had been questioned by police for several hours before the case was classified as no further action (NFA). “I totally understand that the police investigated based on Caprice’s complaint.

items.title: Drug addict numbers hit 130,307 as of June says home minister
items.summary: BENTONG, Oct 5 — A total of 130,307 drug addicts were recorded in the country as of June, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He saId Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah, and Perlis recorded worrying trends in drug use and abuse, exceeding the national ratio of 381 cases per 100,000 population. “For every 100,000 people, Terengganu recorded 735 individuals, while Kelantan recorded 694, Kedah 669, and Perlis 646.

items.title: Audit Dept says 12MP development spending exceeds final allocation by RM6.08b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Overall expenditure on development projects under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) exceeded the final allocation of RM391.776 billion by RM6.076 billion, according to the National Audit Department. In a statement on the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 released today, the department said an audit of the implementation of development projects under RMK-12 found that total development expenditure amounted to RM397.852 billion. “Additional allocations were approved for individual projects whose expenditure exceeded their initial allocations,” the report said.

items.title: Health ministry: 3,025 offered places in ILKKM pre-service programme
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, 5 Okt (Bernama) -- Some 3,025 new trainees have been offered places in the pre-service programme at the Ministry of Health Malaysia Training Institutes (ILKKM) for the October 2026 intake. In a statement today, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said 2,995 of the 3,025 offers were made through the Public Services Commission (SPA), while 30 were for statutory bodies, representing 90.7 per cent of its total quota of 3,335 places. "The Diploma in Nursing programme has the highest intake quota for this session, with 1,818 candidates offered places,” the statement said.
